status: cross-layer transfer executed — 4x4 grid, validated before scaling
split: calibration (74 prompts), fixed across every cell
strength_convention: alpha_ij(z) = z * sigma_ij, sigma_ij = pooled within-group sd of the TARGET layer's activations projected onto the SOURCE direction (construction split). Cells compared at matched z = +8, not matched raw alpha.
direction_normalization: each source direction is unit-norm, matching the layer-wise experiment

requirement_8_dimension_check.enforced_by: check_dimension_compatibility, which raises on mismatch because Causalab would silently broadcast

within_group_sigma_by_source_along_each_._note: rows = target, cols = source; diagonal is the cell's own direction

requirement_9_coordinate_systems.conclusion: residual streams are the same width but the directions are near-orthogonal across depth, and the target layer varies 2-20x less along a foreign axis. Per-cell dose calibration is therefore required; a shared alpha would have delivered a tiny off-diagonal dose and produced an uninterpretable null.

results_at_z_plus_8.reading: same-layer effects are ~6.3x larger in mean absolute magnitude than cross-layer. Every diagonal cell is significant; 8 of 12 off-diagonal cells are also significant but with much smaller effects.

20_26_pair.reading: the only source pair with meaningful cosine. The two directions transfer to each other with OPPOSITE sign, consistent with shared structure expressed in a rotated basis rather than a shared coordinate.

interpretation.successful_behavioural_transfer: the 4 same-layer references plus 8 significant off-diagonal cells, all smaller than their same-layer reference
interpretation.failed_transfer_possible_misalignment: 4 cells (4->20, 4->26, 20->4, 26->4) show no detectable effect at calibrated dose. These are the pairs with the lowest direction cosine (0.009-0.013). This is CONSISTENT with misalignment but does NOT show the feature is absent at those targets.
interpretation.intervention_induced_degradation: 20->20 dropped original-answer accuracy by 0.135 with no rise in target-answer rate: the strongest same-layer intervention disrupts the computation without redirecting it
interpretation.inconclusive: 8 cells are significant but below half the same-layer reference magnitude, so they are reported as partial rather than successful
explicit_limits: A failed transfer does not show the feature is absent from the target layer.
A successful transfer shows behavioural effect, not a uniquely interpretable feature.

z_axis_mismatch.cause: collect_cells selected each cell's largest raw alpha; because dose is calibrated per cell, raw alphas are unrelated across the grid, so cells were compared at different z
z_axis_mismatch.fix: index by z, recovering it as alpha/sigma_ij; selection and comparison happen in z-space

z_match_tolerance.cause: sigma_ij is persisted rounded to 8 decimals, so the recovered z differs from the requested 8 in the last bits; exact comparison dropped every cell
z_match_tolerance.fix: match z with a 1e-3 tolerance and pick the nearest

limitations: 4x4 grid only; an exhaustive 28x28 sweep was deliberately not launched
74 calibration prompts; CIs are wide and 8 cells land in 'inconclusive' partly because of that
single model, single task, one component, one token position
no norm-matched random control arm in this experiment, unlike the layer-wise one, so a cross-layer effect cannot yet be separated from generic perturbation of that size
effect metric is logit margin; target-answer rate is ~0 in every cell, so behavioural transfer is not observed even where representational transfer is
next_steps: add a norm-matched random control arm per cell, as done for the layer-wise experiment
densify the grid around the 20/26 pair, the only region showing off-diagonal structure
scale to more layers only after the control arm is in place
test whether the null pairs are misalignment or insufficient dose by sweeping z upward at 4->20
